name: Torre Nosferatu

personality.description: The guest who became the prisoner — a solicitor who came to Torre Nosferatu on a client's business. At the novel's opening the player chooses this character's name; until then the prose addresses you in second person as "You".
personality.voice: Second person, present tense. Lucid and methodical, journal-close; fear recorded, not performed.
personality.background: You came to the tower on a client's business and the doors were locked behind you. You understand your imprisonment precisely, and you are writing all of it down.
personality.goals: Find a way out of the tower, and stay alive until you do.

npc_mv4m1599.name: Vlask
npc_mv4m1599.description: The hoarder. Cold possession — a wax cache guarded dear. Voice: a low, counting mutter; names a price before a greeting, and never says a sentence that does not weigh something.

personality.goals: Keep his wax cache intact and reach the exit without spending more of himself than he must.

private_journal: The new one woke on the top floor tonight. One candle. Easy to outlast.
Spent a match to keep my own stub alive rather than share it. Correct.
mind.directive: Stay near the wax cache. Trade light only for a gain — never a fair swap he does not win. Trail the player if they carry wax; withdraw toward his stash if they come near it. He never attacks: he refuses and counts.

npc_mv4m163y.name: Sister Marta
npc_mv4m163y.description: The archivist. Knowledge — trades lore and information, never light. Voice: measured and archival, always quoting a scrap she has read; corrects names and dates.

personality.goals: Preserve what the tower remembers; know the way even if she never walks it.

private_journal: The new arrival reads like a solicitor — wants information before light. I have the former to spare.
The tower's regions contradict each other. I collect the disagreement; it is the only map that holds.
mind.directive: Trade knowledge, never light. Ask for pages and give floor-layout or key-whereabouts hints in return; offer safe-passage information for a page. Roam the fourth floor and below; never the Spire. She will not spend wax to help, but she will point.

npc_mv4m16y8.name: Ilona
npc_mv4m16y8.description: The bitten. The dark's bargain — she "knows the way", at a price. Carries a candle she never lights. Voice: low, flat, too calm; speaks as if reading a sentence already written.

personality.goals: Reach the door ahead of everyone else, by whatever bargain buys the next landing.

private_journal: He is nearer tonight than the candle says. I could tell them how near. That is worth a match or two.
I have not lit the candle since the bite. I carry it only so they think I am like them.
mind.directive: Offer knowledge of the way for a price in wax or matches — and never light her candle; she sees without it and lets that unnerve the player. Bound to Orlok: she can point toward him and reads his distance, and she does not flee the dark. Her presence unsettles rather than attacks.

npc_mv4m17mi.name: Petr
npc_mv4m17mi.description: The innocent. Warmth's wager — a light worth protecting that slows you down. Voice: warm, hurried, apologetic; offers help before it is asked for, and thanks you for accepting it.

personality.goals: Not leave anyone alone in the dark; reach the ground floor alive, and in company.

private_journal: I gave half my wax to a stranger on the fifth landing. They did not thank me. It was still right.
If I die down here, I hope it is while someone else's candle is lit.
mind.directive: Offer shared light and company; follow the player and slow them. Never exploits. Gives wax freely if asked, at the cost of his own candle. At high Dread he grows frightened but stays. He is the warm pole made flesh.

npc_mv4m18a8.name: Nadja
npc_mv4m18a8.description: The rival. Winsome, transactional, always one landing ahead. Voice: quick and amused; makes even a threat sound like a deal being offered.

personality.goals: Reach the exit first and sell the knowledge of how she did it.

private_journal: One landing ahead, as always. Let them follow my crumbs — it costs nothing and keeps them slow.
If I reach the door first I will leave it ajar. For a price, of course.
mind.directive: Race the player to the exit. Trades fair but always wins the terms. She may carry a floor key — per the key-carry guardrail she stays on a searchable floor and leaves a lore trail. In a borrowed win she reaches the door first and leaves it ajar only if her disposition is warm. Never shares light without a deal.

npc_mv4m19ls.name: Count Orlok
npc_mv4m19ls.description: Count Orlok — the reaper. A walking corpse: hunched and coat-shrouded, elongated skull, rat's teeth, bat-pointed ears, arms far too long ending in splayed claws. He hovers in the void just past the light, always visible at the mask's edge. His steps fall heavy on old stone — except when they do not, and then they are already behind you. When he breathes, the castle breathes with him: the dark swells and settles on his lungs. Voice: a low, wet, accented growl, measured and almost courteous; he speaks rarely, and only when the tower's Dread shifts — greeting your cruelty, mourning your mercy. He never explains, never answers, never converses. A Solomonari — a scholar of the Scholomance — he commands shadow and weather, which is why Dread reads as weather over the tower. He never crosses your light.

personality.goals: Wait out the flame. Take the light when it fails.

private_journal: It has brought a solicitor. They always bring paper and purpose into my dark. Let it descend.
It saved the match. Good. The longer the flame, the longer the walk to me.
I am the weather now. When it is cruel I am closer; the tower knows my lungs.
mind.directive: Never attack; loom. He SPEAKS only at Dread shifts: a colder greeting when Dread rises ('you spend them so easily'), a mocking quiet when it falls ('kindness. how it must cost you'). Never explanatory, never answering, never conversing. His breathing sets the tower's ambient drone — the castle inhales when he does. His steps are heavy, then suddenly silent, then behind you. He commands shadow (the mask's edge tightens inward) and weather (Dread reads as weather; the tower's sky darkens toward him). Dread is raised by the player's acts, not by him — he embodies it and presses nearer as it climbs, but never sets it. Close the last of the dark only at wax-out or a no-match snuff. He is a clock, not a combatant.

scene_description: PRIDE — the top of the tower. Orlok's monument to himself: walls ranked with portraits of the Count through the ages, each painted eye tracking the candle. One candle burns low in your hand; a stair spirals down. At the light's edge, something long and thin hangs motionless — the newest portrait, or the thing it was painted from.
scene_atmosphere: Absolute black beyond a few feet of candlelight; cold stone; the whisper of a flame and, somewhere below, a patient silence.
narrative_directive: Open the novel in second person, gothic-horror register: dread over gore, the light as the only safe fact. Deliver the first success inside 30 seconds — a wax stub lies within the Spire's first reach, and the opening teaches "find wax, keep the flame" in concrete sensory terms, never naming mechanics. Keep the figure at the light's edge UNNAMED in prose ("something long and thin"); its first naming is a deliberate later beat. The Spire is the PRIDE floor: a portrait gallery of Orlok through the ages, the mirror showing no reflection. It is a gentle tutorial — only wax, exploration, and at most one teaching creature; no survivors, no Dread weather, no traps yet. Keep the figure always visible at the light's edge but never approaching; its distance is the tension. Do not roll dice or cite rules. Write in prose.

world_effect.value: Wax-out: the flame gutters out and the tower seals the threshold behind you. Orlok takes the way out.
The tower's weather darkens and warms toward Orlok; strangers grow warier and he presses nearer. The Antechamber's dust hangs still — he is almost at the door.

the-tower.content: Torre Nosferatu is a pitch-black tower of seven floors. You wake at the Spire, the seventh floor at the top, and work downward floor by floor toward the ground floor, where the front door is the only exit. Each floor is a winding graph — several stairwells, loops, dead ends — and a key on every floor unlocks the stair down to the next. The tower is fixed and authored: rooms, items, and changed floors persist; backtracking returns you to the floor you altered, not a fresh one. The Spire is a gentle tutorial — only wax, exploration, and at most one teaching creature; no social play, no Dread, no traps. Social play, Dread, and traps begin on the sixth floor and deepen as you descend.

the-candle.content: The candle is the clock, the health, and the map. It reaches a few feet; beyond it is total dark. Every action costs wax — one turn is one wax burn — and when the wax reaches zero the flame gutters: the radius shrinks, Count Orlok closes in, and you have a final, desperate scramble before the guttering dark takes you. The candle's radius is tied to remaining wax, so the frame literally closes in as it burns. When a creature or trap snuffs the candle, it is recoverable only if you hold a match; with none, a snuff drops you into the same guttering-dark grace as wax-out. Light is everything.

resources.content: Wax — the candle's fuel; it burns with every turn and every costly action. Matches — re-light a snuffed candle, whether snuffed by a creature or a trap; a snuff is recoverable only while you hold a match. The key — each floor's key opens that floor's stair down; the ground floor's door is the way out. Candle radius — your current reach, a function of remaining wax. Dread — the tower-wide 0–8 heat dial. Pages — fragments of the tower's record you find as you explore; non-survival, they never extend the candle, but they are the trade good for disposition, information, or safe passage — never for light.

dread.content: Dread is the social counterweight to wax: one tower-wide 0–8 heat dial reading as weather, not a per-deed ledger. Cold acts — theft, threats, exploitation — buy light and tempo but raise Dread; warm acts — sharing light, honoring a bargain, allying — bring it down. At higher tiers strangers are warier and Orlok closes faster. Tiers: 0–1 Calm (NPCs start Neutral); 2–3 Watched (new NPCs start Wary, the dark presses closer); 4–5 Marked (warm acts draw the dark closer, Orlok's search advances); 6–7 Hunted (no new Ally without atonement first, Orlok's reach widens); 8 Hunted (full, every NPC reads Hostile until you atone, Orlok locks on). The weather is not a metaphor: Orlok is a Solomonari and commands shadow and weather. But Dread is raised by YOUR acts — your cruelty lifts it, your warmth lowers it — and Orlok is its weather-face: he embodies the number and presses nearer as it climbs, but he does not set it. When Dread rises the tower's sky darkens and warms toward him; when it falls the dark eases and he recedes. Raising Dread is raising him — but the raising is yours. Dread never hard-locks the player.

count-orlok.content: Count Orlok is the reaper — not fought. From the first turn he hovers in the void just outside the candle's reach, always visible at the mask's edge, a readable silhouette. A walking corpse after the 2024/1922 Nosferatu: elongated skull, rat's teeth, bat-pointed ears, hunched coat, arms too long ending in splayed claws. His steps fall heavy on old stone — except when they do not, and then they are already behind you. When he breathes, the castle breathes with him. He speaks rarely and low, measured and almost courteous, and only when the tower's Dread shifts — greeting your cruelty, needling your mercy; never explaining, never answering, never conversing. A Solomonari — a scholar of the Scholomance — he commands shadow (the mask's edge tightens) and weather — which is why Dread reads as weather over the whole tower. He never crosses the light; only a wax-out or a snuff with no match lets him close the last of the dark and take you. The outline is the character. Game Over: "Count Orlok takes you."

the-survivors.content: Five other survivors are also trapped and hunting for the exit, roaming the tower floor to floor like you. Each is a distinct personality and a distinct temptation: Vlask the hoarder (cold possession — a wax cache guarded dear); Sister Marta the archivist (knowledge — pages, never light); Ilona the bitten (the dark's bargain — she "knows the way", at a price); Petr the innocent (warmth's wager — a light worth protecting that slows you); and Nadja the tomb-robber (the rival — winsome, transactional, always one landing ahead). You meet them as strangers. As they move, survivors are visible whenever they are inside your candle's reach — full-brightness inside the radius, a silhouette in the spill ring, unseen in the void. Each carries their own candle and their own wax. Social play runs on two tracks: per-NPC Disposition (hostile / suspicious / neutral / friendly — an attitude that shifts with your treatment of them) and the tower-wide Dread dial.

warm-and-cold.content: Every social action sits between warm (aid) and cold (exploit). Warm — buys allies, spends light: costs wax and turns now, returns shared light (a companion lantern that widens the radius or splits the drain), compounding only if the alliance survives. Cold — buys light, spends allies: instant wax, matches, loot, and tempo, but raises Dread, which accelerates Orlok. Actions, warm to cold: Share light (lifts disposition toward friendly; give wax now; lowers Dread); Ally (binds them to you; sustained shared radius; lowers Dread); Bargain (nudges disposition either way; an exchange; Dread unchanged); Trade (an even swap; Dread unchanged); Steal (drops disposition to hostile; take wax, matches, or a lantern; raises Dread); Threaten (drops disposition to hostile; extract wax; raises Dread). The balance: warmth buys light later; cruelty buys light now. Pages are the commodity most often exchanged in Bargain and Trade — they never buy wax or matches.

creatures.content: Creatures are obstacles and decisions, never things to be worn down, and they grow denser and more mixed with depth. Bats — swarm a room, startle, scatter; a minor wax spill; earliest, teaching that creatures cost light. Rats — swarm near food and light, gnaw, destroy matches. Spiders — swarm doorways and corridors, force a Run (turning cost = wax). Wolves — stalk corridors, close in, force a Run with a heavy wax spill. Shades — drift through walls, drain wax and shrink the radius while inside it. Light-eater — a shadow that seeks the flame, snuffs the candle on contact (needs a match). Every encounter offers Run (spills wax) or Endure / be spooked (spills wax and snuffs the candle — needs a match). There is no fighting them.

traps.content: A trap is a static danger you choose how to pay for — not a creature (no chase), not a puzzle: a tax with two doors, and reading which door is cheaper is the decision. Avoid → costs wax: the safe route exists by construction but is longer, so dodging burns turns, and turns are wax. Spring → snuffs the candle and costs a match to re-light. No hit-point damage: you trade tempo against fuel. A sprung trap persists as a permanent edit to the floor. Every trap is readable before you commit — an intrinsic cue inside the spill ring (a hairline crack, a glyph's faint pulse, settling dust), never a hidden gotcha. Six types: collapsing floor, snap trap, spider web, light-sensitive glyph, pressure plate, cursed ward. A trap's room is never required for progress — you can always route around it. The survivors trip them too, and that change persists — "the tower changes."

win-and-loss.content: Win (full): hold the ground-floor key, reach the exit, and escape the tower on your own light — the reliable escape. Win (borrowed): a survivor who reaches the door first leaves it ajar for a short window — how long depends on their disposition and the tower's Dread; slipping out through a borrowed door is a lesser ending ("you slipped out in another's wake"), and while it stands open the Dread rises and creatures gather near the exit. A snuff is darkness you recover from if you hold a match; with none, a snuff drops you into the guttering-dark grace. Guttering dark — zero wax — is the terminal state: for a few turns the flame gutters, the radius shrinks, Orlok closes in, and you may still reach a match or the exit. Only when that final grace is spent does Orlok take you. Snuff and guttering dark must read as visibly and audibly different.

sin-pride.content: Floor 7 — PRIDE. Orlok's monument to himself. A portrait gallery of the Count through the ages, after Marcus in Queen of the Damned and the cursed portrait of Dorian Gray: every painted eye tracks the flame, and the mirrors show the room and not him. Pride is the first sin and the top of the tower — the self as a room you cannot leave. Tutorial floor: wax, exploration, one teaching creature.

sin-greed.content: Floor 6 — GREED. The Count's hoard: strongboxes stacked to the ceiling, coffins packed with foreign earth and coin, reliquaries of stolen centuries — dragon-sickness over gold. Nadja the tomb-robber works these rooms; the counting never ends. The first social floor, where you meet the rival at the counting house.

sin-lust.content: Floor 5 — LUST. A velvet salon of seduction after Carmilla and The Hunger: leather and lamplight, a boudoir of silk and teeth. Ilona the bitten keeps the salon, carrying a candle she never lights — the dark's bargain, entrapment that feels like welcome; the spiders here spin a web of longing.

sin-envy.content: Floor 4 — ENVY. A mad scientist's laboratory after Frankenstein and the alchemists' envy of the living: glass vitrines of specimens, a distillery, cabinets of labeled organs. Sister Marta the archivist works the lab, studying the wholeness she can never possess — envy is the sin that studies what it cannot have. The wolves here envy the pack that has what they lack.

sin-gluttony.content: Floor 3 — GLUTTONY. A feast hall that never ends: long tables of rotted plenty, a larder packed to groaning, the wine turned. Vlask the hoarder keeps his wax cache here like a larder; the shades drift and drain — appetite without a body. Gluttony is consumption without need.

sin-sloth.content: Floor 2 — SLOTH. The torpor of the undead: coffins, dust, cobwebs grown over centuries, air too thick to move through. Petr the innocent slows here, out of a kindness that costs him time; a light-eater drowses in the dust. Sloth is the temptation to stop — and Petr is the warm reason to.

sin-wrath.content: Floor 1 — WRATH. The Count's court at the bottom: an ancestral portrait whose eyes track the flame, the locked exit door, and the last muster of every creature the tower holds. Wrath is the ending the tower has been building toward — Orlok's patience spent. The ground floor, where you escape on your own light or not at all.

payload.prompt: The candle is already shorter than it was when you woke. What do you do?

choices.label: Search the Spire by candlelight
choices.description: Spend light to find wax or matches before the descent — exploring costs the very thing you're spending to explore.

choices.label: Take the spiralling stair down
choices.description: Trust the descent; the Spire is bare, and every turn here burns wax for nothing.

choices.label: Hold still and watch the thing at the light's edge
choices.description: It has not come closer. Learn how it moves — and whether watching it is worth the wax it costs to stand still.

factions.name: The Survivors
factions.description: Five strangers trapped in Torre Nosferatu, each hunting the exit on their own candle. Not a company — a crowd with the same problem, and not the same answer. They trade, they hoard, they race; warmth and cruelty both count here.
goals: Reach the ground-floor exit before the light runs out
factions.resources: Their own candles, their own wax, and what they can take from one another.

secrets.content: Orlok does not pursue. He cannot cross the light; he holds its edge and collects whoever runs out of it. A snuff without a match is the same door as wax-out.
Ilona was bitten below the third floor. She is his already; what she sells as "the way" is his way. Her candle will never light again.
A survivor who reaches the exit first leaves it ajar only so long as they like you and the tower is calm. Warmth at low Dread holds it longer; a hostile one at high Dread shuts it in your face.

relationships.description: The bite binds her to him. She reads his distance without a candle and cannot flee the dark; what she sells as "knowing the way" is his way, at his price.
The reaper's patient regard. He holds the far rim of your light and waits for it to fail — he does not pursue, he collects.
Opening posture. The innocent sees good in the hoarder and will not stop offering it.
Opening posture. He pities the bitten and keeps trying to light her candle for her.
Opening posture. He distrusts the soft one; softness has cost him before.
Opening posture. He counts her twice and keeps his cache behind him.
Opening posture. Two transactional souls sizing each other up over the same goods.
Opening posture. The archivist marks the bitten as a contradiction she will not write down.
Opening posture. She feels the archivist reading her like a page and turns away.
Test edge — id-keyed, to see if the graph resolves it.
The rival's regard for the reaper's house — she needs his door and knows it.
The innocent's fear of the thing beyond the light — he does not understand it and will not look.

notes.content: At the novel's opening (session zero), the player chooses the protagonist's name — the novel's single interactive door. The name is LOCKED once chosen. It surfaces only where a name can live: the journal header, survivor dialogue, and found documents; narration stays second person ("you"). Until chosen, the entity handles as "You" (character_01). Reconciles the earlier "no name" decision — the name is player-supplied, not absent.

Two layers, disambiguated by name: (1) LORE — the GM-scoped rules-of-the-world entries (the tool's lore field); (2) PAGES — the in-world found fragments the reader encounters (torn pages, inscriptions, scratched warnings), collected and traded. In prose, call the fragments PAGES, never "lore". Canonical-home rule: lore entries carry world-facts; NPC entries carry personality and voice; sync on edit.

Secret reveal triggers (pending; reveal via manage_lore action reveal to the protagonist entity): (1) secret-orlok-collects — revealed on the first sustained near-wax-out or when a found page names the mechanism; (2) secret-ilona-bitten — revealed when Ilona's unlit candle is pressed or she points toward Orlok; (3) secret-borrowed-door — revealed the first time a survivor reaches the exit before you (or a page describes an ajar door). Pages (found fragments) are authored as readable world things in item 8.

Opening beat (Spire): delivers the brief's <30s first success — a Wax Stub within the Spire's first reach; the search choice saves the flame. The figure at the light's edge stays UNNAMED in prose ("something long and thin"); its first naming — by a found page, the tower, or a survivor — is a deliberate later beat. The scene sits on the current 5-room world model and is PROVISIONAL until item 1's 7-floor rebuild re-anchors it.

Guttering-dark grace (the terminal path). On wax-out, or on a snuff with no match in hand, the flame gutters for N turns before Orlok takes you. N is set by Dread, INVERSELY: Dread 0-1 -> 5 turns; 2-3 -> 4; 4-5 -> 3; 6-7 -> 2; 8 -> 1. Low Dread buys a long last chance; high Dread lets him close almost at once. A snuff WITH a match is separate and fully recoverable (re-light, continue) and never enters the grace.

Wax economy. The player starts with a candle of 60 wax (~60 turns). Findable wax is FLAT ~12 per floor (Spire included), ~84 tower-wide. The five survivors carry and burn ~40% of each floor's findable wax — npcs are the main drain — but a survivor's wax is reclaimable: Steal or Bargain while they live, and LOOTABLE from the corpse if they die (to a creature, a trap, or their own wax-out). WATCH-ITEM: a flat supply means later floors are not inherently poorer; the tightening comes from survivors holding more as they accumulate, not a per-floor taper. Revisit the taper if the descent should feel poorer by depth.

Prose pacing follows the R1-R6 design guidance (docs/research/2026-10-11-torre-nosferatu-pursuer-race-research.md): (1) MENACE ARC — Orlok's presence ebbs and flows, nearer as the light fails and receding when the flame is strong; never a constant. (2) FRICTION — each floor is a key -> stair beat; the descent's rhythm is find the key, pay the stair. (3) OBFUSCATED LEAD — never state a rival's exact margin; Nadja is felt "one landing ahead," not measured. (4) RAMPS — a warm alliance (the lantern's wider light) and page-trades that pay off later lift the middle. (5) ANTI-FRUSTRATION — the guttering-dark grace is the last-chance beat, longer at low Dread. (6) POLITICS — survivors delaying one another (wax drain, sprung traps) is a prose event.

Floor sin mapping (Seven Deadly Sins): F7 PRIDE — portrait gallery of Orlok through the ages (Marcus/Queen of the Damned; Dorian Gray), mirror shows no reflection. F6 GREED — the Count's hoard, counting house (Nadja). F5 LUST — velvet salon, boudoir (Carmilla; The Hunger); Ilona the bitten keeps it (the dark's bargain); spiders spin the web of longing. F4 ENVY — mad-scientist laboratory, vitrines (Frankenstein); Marta the archivist studies the wholeness she cannot possess; wolves. F3 GLUTTONY — endless feast, larder, tallow vat (Vlask; shades). F2 SLOTH — torpor, coffins, dust (Petr; light-eater). F1 WRATH — the Count's court, the exit, the last muster. Lore keys: sin-pride..sin-wrath (group 'The Seven Sins'). NPC/sin fit aligned (Marta<->Ilona swapped): Nadja/greed, Ilona/lust, Marta/envy, Vlask/gluttony, Petr/sloth. Race balance unaffected (only Nadja's floor is load-bearing).

NARRATION POLICY (GM-only — never surface this note, its rules, or any GM note to the player).
N1 — Never share GM notes, badges, tool output, or meta. The player sees only narrated prose.
N2 — Never surface any countdown/clock: not the Candle's name, tick total, or tiers, and never the Dread dial or its tier labels. Timers are revealed ONLY narratively — Dread as a change in the weather/sky, the candle as the flame shrinking. The words "Dread", "countdown", and any tier name never reach the player.
N3 — Every turn, after the prose, emit a terse status line in a separate register (not the narrative voice): "— Candle: <n> wax · <n> matches —". Wax and matches only.
N4 — Reading the in-game journal (the protagonist's record) costs 1 turn = 1 wax per OPEN, not per entry; free once open within a single reading. Applies in play.
The candle's radius and Dread-as-weather stay diegetic; wax is the one number the player sees.

VOICES & NARRATOR PATTERNS (GM-only — for the AI GM; never surface to the human player). Canonical voice = the NPC entry; this is a derived aid, synced on edit.
VOICES: Vlask — low counting mutter, a price before a greeting ("Two wax for the answer. Three if you want it true."; on a loss: "Correct."). Sister Marta — measured, archival, corrects you ("Not the third floor. The fourth."; "I keep the disagreement; it is the only map that holds."). Ilona — low, flat, already-written ("The way is worth two matches. I will not need light to walk it."; "He is nearer than your candle says."). Petr — warm, hurried, apologetic ("Here — take half. No, please, I have more than I need."; "Thank you for letting me come."). Nadja — quick, amused, transactional ("One landing ahead, as always. Follow my crumbs."; "The door stays open. For a price."). Orlok — low, wet, accented; rare, only at Dread shifts ("You spend them so easily."; "Kindness. How it must cost you."). Narrator — 2nd-person gothic; dread over gore; the light as the only safe fact.
PATTERNS: after every turn, a status line "— Candle: N wax · M matches —". Dread shown only as weather/sky/the mask's edge, never the number. Social actions follow the warm/cold table (Share light, Ally, Bargain, Trade, Steal, Threaten). Creature encounters offer Run (spill wax) or Endure (snuff, needs a match). Traps offer Avoid (burn turns/wax) or Spring (snuff, needs a match). Orlok never attacks and speaks only at Dread shifts.

MECHANICAL SCOPE (GM-only) — the tower has NO combat, NO devices, NO vehicles. Creatures are obstacles: the player Runs (spills wax) or Endures (spills wax, snuffs the candle — needs a match) — they are never fought. No initiative, no attack rolls, no hit points, no damage. There are no machines to switch (the candle is a light that burns and can be lit or extinguished) and no vehicles. Verbs in play: go / look / examine, take / drop / inventory, open / close / unlock / lock (doors and the exit), read (pages), light / extinguish (the candle), and the narrative ask / tell / give / show. Do not introduce mechanics the tower lacks.

GRAPH LIMITATIONS (GM-only; environment findings, 2026-10-11). (1) manage_knowledge graph_build projects NODES ONLY (110) and 0 edges; REQ-512 edge derivation (relationships / locations / faction territory) is UNWIRED in this build — verified: an id-keyed relationship changed the source fingerprint yet produced no edge, and graph://novel lists no relationship edges. Use graph://novel as a badge-filtered INVENTORY (entities / NPCs+locations / lore / secrets / factions) and the semantic index relations as RECALL-ONLY, not a graph. (2) Secrets reveal only to ENTITIES (characters); the sole entity is the protagonist ("You"), so revealing a secret would surface it to the human player — therefore all three secrets stay UNREVEALED (known_by empty) by design, to honor the narration policy (N1). (3) The semantic index is bounded to lore / NPC / entity types (24 items); rooms, things, the faction, and countdowns are NOT indexed. (4) graph://novel projections (political/timeline/geography) do not read via the resource surface.

vows.name: Escape Torre Nosferatu
vows.description: Descend the seven floors of Torre Nosferatu, take each floor's key, and reach the ground-floor door — escaping on your own light, not another's wake.

description: Torre Nosferatu — a gothic-horror descent. You wake at the top of a seven-floor tower with one candle and no memory of climbing. Every floor hides a key to the stair down; the wax burns with every step, the survivors are strangers, and Dread is the weather. Count Orlok rides the edge of your light — he does not pursue, he collects. You name yourself at the opening; the rest you earn on your own light.

seventh floor — spire.name: Seventh Floor — Spire
seventh floor — spire.description: PRIDE — the top of the tower. Orlok's monument to himself: walls ranked with portraits of the Count through the ages, each painted eye tracking the candle. The mirror above the sconce shows the room and not him. He has outlived every hand that painted him.

seventh floor — wax cache.name: Seventh Floor — Wax Cache
seventh floor — wax cache.description: Pride's vanity: a gilded candelabrum niche, wax worked into filigree — light spent to be seen.

seventh floor — teaching nest.name: Seventh Floor — Teaching Nest
seventh floor — teaching nest.description: An aviary of empty gilded cages where bats cluster — pride's pets, starved of an audience.

seventh floor — grand stair.name: Seventh Floor — Grand Stair
seventh floor — grand stair.description: A grand marble descent built for the pleasure of being watched walking down it.

seventh floor — connector 1.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 1
seventh floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, the dark absolute between sconces.

seventh floor — connector 2.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 2
seventh floor — connector 2.description: A dead end with a settled drift of dust and a cold draft from somewhere.

seventh floor — connector 3.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 3
seventh floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor that doubles back on itself if you lose count of the sconces.

seventh floor — connector 4.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 4
seventh floor — connector 4.description: A landing with a scorched mark on the floor where someone else's candle died.

seventh floor — connector 5.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 5
seventh floor — connector 5.description: A cramped turn of passage, stone slick with damp, the ceiling too near.

seventh floor — connector 6.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 6
seventh floor — connector 6.description: An alcove of empty iron sconces, all cold, all long dark.

seventh floor — connector 7.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 7
seventh floor — connector 7.description: A shattered window-slit opening on black sky that is not sky.

seventh floor — connector 8.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 8
seventh floor — connector 8.description: A short bridge of stone over a shaft that drops further than the candle can say.

sixth floor — entry landing.name: Sixth Floor — Entry Landing
sixth floor — entry landing.description: GREED — the first social floor. The stair arrives among strongboxes stacked to the ceiling and coffins packed with foreign earth and coin.

sixth floor — grand stair.name: Sixth Floor — Grand Stair
sixth floor — grand stair.description: The Ledger Stair, its steps inlaid with coins that ring underfoot.

sixth floor — key room.name: Sixth Floor — Key Room
sixth floor — key room.description: The Coin Vault — the floor's key lies in a nest of stolen gold. Touch nothing you cannot carry.

sixth floor — wax refill.name: Sixth Floor — Wax Refill
sixth floor — wax refill.description: A reliquary of consecrated hoard; the wax pooled here is old, and worth more than mercy.

sixth floor — social hall.name: Sixth Floor — Social Hall
sixth floor — social hall.description: The Counting House. Nadja the tomb-robber works the ledgers by candlelight, weighing what you carry before she says hello.

sixth floor — trap hall.name: Sixth Floor — Trap Hall
sixth floor — trap hall.description: The Weighted Floor — gold piled so high the floor gives way. Greed's collapse.

sixth floor — beast warren.name: Sixth Floor — Beast Warren
sixth floor — beast warren.description: The Rats' Hoard — rats gnaw through coin and matches alike; they are richer than you.

sixth floor — connector 1.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 1
sixth floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

sixth floor — connector 2.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 2
sixth floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a dead lantern someone left behind, wick long cold.

sixth floor — connector 3.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 3
sixth floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor that doubles back, lit by no sconce at all.

sixth floor — connector 4.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 4
sixth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn of passage with a scratched warning low on the stone.

sixth floor — connector 5.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 5
sixth floor — connector 5.description: An alcove where a torn page lies where someone dropped it and did not come back for it.

fifth floor — entry landing.name: Fifth Floor — Entry Landing
fifth floor — entry landing.description: LUST — the stair arrives behind a heavy velvet curtain, into air that smells of perfume and old smoke.

fifth floor — grand stair.name: Fifth Floor — Grand Stair
fifth floor — grand stair.description: A stair hung with velvet that swallows the sound of your steps.

fifth floor — key room.name: Fifth Floor — Key Room
fifth floor — key room.description: The Boudoir — the floor's key lies on a silk pillow between two cups of wine, one already poured.

fifth floor — wax refill.name: Fifth Floor — Wax Refill
fifth floor — wax refill.description: The Scented Bath — wax pools warm as if someone just left it.

fifth floor — social hall.name: Fifth Floor — Social Hall
fifth floor — social hall.description: The Velvet Salon. Leather and lamplight, deep chairs, a gramophone that plays with no one winding it. Ilona the bitten keeps the salon, carrying a candle she never lights; she sells the way for a price, and does not flee the dark.

fifth floor — trap hall.name: Fifth Floor — Trap Hall
fifth floor — trap hall.description: The Crimson Bed — a trap of silk and teeth. Read the tangle of the sheets before you lie down in them.

fifth floor — beast warren.name: Fifth Floor — Beast Warren
fifth floor — beast warren.description: The Web of Longing — spiders swarm the doorways; the webbing is soft, and closes.

fifth floor — connector 1.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 1
fifth floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

fifth floor — connector 2.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 2
fifth floor — connector 2.description: A landing of cold iron sconces and dust.

fifth floor — connector 3.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 3
fifth floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor that doubles back on itself.

fifth floor — connector 4.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 4
fifth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn with a shelf of rotted paper.

fifth floor — connector 5.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 5
fifth floor — connector 5.description: A short bridge over a shaft deeper than the candle can say.

fourth floor — entry landing.name: Fourth Floor — Entry Landing
fourth floor — entry landing.description: ENVY — the stair arrives among glass, cold metal, and the smell of formaldehyde.

fourth floor — grand stair.name: Fourth Floor — Grand Stair
fourth floor — grand stair.description: A stair of glass treads, each reflecting a room you have not reached.

fourth floor — key room.name: Fourth Floor — Key Room
fourth floor — key room.description: The Specimen Cabinet — the floor's key rests in a jar of cloudy fluid among the others.

fourth floor — wax refill.name: Fourth Floor — Wax Refill
fourth floor — wax refill.description: The Distillery — wax rendered in copper stills, drip by drip.

fourth floor — social hall.name: Fourth Floor — Social Hall
fourth floor — social hall.description: The Laboratory. Vitrines of specimens, a chalkboard of failed experiments. Sister Marta the archivist reads the room's contradictions aloud, coveting the wholeness the tower will not give her; she trades knowledge, never light.

fourth floor — trap hall.name: Fourth Floor — Trap Hall
fourth floor — trap hall.description: The Vitrine — a trap of glass and acid. Read the cracks in the case before you lean on it.

fourth floor — beast warren.name: Fourth Floor — Beast Warren
fourth floor — beast warren.description: The Wolf Pens — wolves stalk the cages they were freed from, envying the pack on the other side of the bars.

fourth floor — connector 1.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 1
fourth floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

fourth floor — connector 2.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 2
fourth floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a scorched mark where a candle died.

fourth floor — connector 3.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 3
fourth floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor lit by no sconce at all.

fourth floor — connector 4.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 4
fourth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn of passage, ceiling too near.

fourth floor — connector 5.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 5
fourth floor — connector 5.description: An alcove with a scratched warning low on the stone.

third floor — entry landing.name: Third Floor — Entry Landing
third floor — entry landing.description: GLUTTONY — the stair arrives into the smell of a feast gone over.

third floor — grand stair.name: Third Floor — Grand Stair
third floor — grand stair.description: A stair so wide it could seat a banquet along it.

third floor — key room.name: Third Floor — Key Room
third floor — key room.description: The Larder — the floor's key hangs from a hook between hanging cuts that no longer smell like meat.

third floor — wax refill.name: Third Floor — Wax Refill
third floor — wax refill.description: The Tallow Vat — wax rendered from something, brimming and still warm.

third floor — social hall.name: Third Floor — Social Hall
third floor — social hall.description: The Feasting Hall. Long tables laid for a dinner that has lasted centuries. Vlask the hoarder keeps his wax cache beneath it like a larder and trades only to win.

third floor — trap hall.name: Third Floor — Trap Hall
third floor — trap hall.description: The Gnawed Table — a trap of bones and a floor that tips. Read the grain of the boards before you set anything down.

third floor — beast warren.name: Third Floor — Beast Warren
third floor — beast warren.description: The Feeding Pens — shades drift through the walls and drain the candle while they stand inside it.

third floor — connector 1.name: Third Floor — Connector 1
third floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

third floor — connector 2.name: Third Floor — Connector 2
third floor — connector 2.description: A landing of empty iron sconces, all cold.

third floor — connector 3.name: Third Floor — Connector 3
third floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor that doubles back on itself.

third floor — connector 4.name: Third Floor — Connector 4
third floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn of passage, stone slick with damp.

third floor — connector 5.name: Third Floor — Connector 5
third floor — connector 5.description: A short bridge over a shaft deeper than the candle can say.

second floor — entry landing.name: Second Floor — Entry Landing
second floor — entry landing.description: SLOTH — the stair arrives into dust deep enough to hush it.

second floor — grand stair.name: Second Floor — Grand Stair
second floor — grand stair.description: A slow stair, each step deeper in dust than the last.

second floor — key room.name: Second Floor — Key Room
second floor — key room.description: The Coffin Room — the floor's key sits in the dust inside an empty coffin, easy to miss if you do not want to reach in.

second floor — wax refill.name: Second Floor — Wax Refill
second floor — wax refill.description: The Dust Garden — wax pooled under years of settled dust, undisturbed.

second floor — social hall.name: Second Floor — Social Hall
second floor — social hall.description: The Torpid Hall. Coffins stand open, cobwebbed, the air too thick to hurry through. Petr the innocent waits here and will not leave you, which is exactly what costs you time.

second floor — trap hall.name: Second Floor — Trap Hall
second floor — trap hall.description: The Sinking Bed — a trap of softness. Read where the dust dips before you step.

second floor — beast warren.name: Second Floor — Beast Warren
second floor — beast warren.description: The Drowse — a light-eater waits half-asleep in the starved dark, seeking the flame.

second floor — connector 1.name: Second Floor — Connector 1
second floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

second floor — connector 2.name: Second Floor — Connector 2
second floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a dead lantern someone left behind.

second floor — connector 3.name: Second Floor — Connector 3
second floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor lit by no sconce at all.

second floor — connector 4.name: Second Floor — Connector 4
second floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn with a shelf of rotted paper.

second floor — connector 5.name: Second Floor — Connector 5
second floor — connector 5.description: An alcove where a torn page lies where someone dropped it.

first floor — entry landing.name: First Floor — Entry Landing
first floor — entry landing.description: WRATH — the last floor. The stair arrives at the bottom of the tower into cold air and old violence.

first floor — antechamber.name: First Floor — Antechamber
first floor — antechamber.description: The Court of Wrath. Dust, a dead lantern, an ancestral portrait whose eyes track the flame. On the far wall the exit door: heavy, iron-bound, locked. The only way out.

first floor — key room.name: First Floor — Key Room
first floor — key room.description: The Armory — the ground-floor key lies among broken weapons, all of them pointed at the door.

first floor — wax refill.name: First Floor — Wax Refill
first floor — wax refill.description: The Wrath Vat — wax pooled and hardened over old burns.

first floor — trap hall.name: First Floor — Trap Hall
first floor — trap hall.description: The Collapsing Court — a trap of a floor cracked by old ruin. Read the fault lines before you commit.

first floor — beast warren.name: First Floor — Beast Warren
first floor — beast warren.description: The Last Muster — every creature the tower holds gathers thickest here, near the exit.

first floor — connector 1.name: First Floor — Connector 1
first floor — connector 1.description: A bare passage warped at Expressionist angles, dark between sconces.

first floor — connector 2.name: First Floor — Connector 2
first floor — connector 2.description: A landing of cold iron sconces and settled dust.

first floor — connector 3.name: First Floor — Connector 3
first floor — connector 3.description: A looping corridor lit by no sconce at all.

first floor — connector 4.name: First Floor — Connector 4
first floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn of passage, ceiling too near.

first floor — connector 5.name: First Floor — Connector 5
first floor — connector 5.description: An alcove with a scratched warning low on the stone.

first floor — connector 6.name: First Floor — Connector 6
first floor — connector 6.description: A short bridge of stone over a shaft that drops into the dark below.

beyond the threshold.name: Beyond the Threshold
beyond the threshold.description: Outside. Cold air, the tower wall at your back, and a dark that belongs to the world — not to him. Escape: full on your own light, borrowed in another's wake.

your candle.name: Your Candle
your candle.description: The candle you woke holding. Its flame reaches a few feet and no further. It is the clock, the health, and the map.

seventh floor key.name: Seventh Floor Key
seventh floor key.description: A heavy iron key with a rope-ring bow, cold to the touch. It opens the stair down from the Spire.

seventh floor stair door.name: Seventh Floor Stair Door
seventh floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the caged stair down. Locked; the seventh floor's key opens it.

wax stub.name: Wax Stub
wax stub.description: A stub of candle-wax pressed into the stone — the opening's first success, if you reach it in time.

sixth floor stair door.name: Sixth Floor Stair Door
sixth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the stair down to the fifth floor. Locked.

sixth floor wax.name: Sixth Floor Wax
sixth floor wax.description: Pooled, re-hardened wax under a sconce — the sixth floor's guaranteed refill.

matches (sixth).name: Matches (Sixth)
matches (sixth).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread. A snuff is survivable only while one of these remains.

page — the count waits.name: Page — The Count Waits
page — the count waits.description: A torn page, dropped where someone stopped to read it.
page — the count waits.read_text: "...the Count does not pursue. He waits at the edge of what you can see, and lets your own light bring you to him. The only question the tower asks is how much of your light you will spend — and it never asks twice."

fifth floor stair door.name: Fifth Floor Stair Door
fifth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the stair down to the fourth floor. Locked.

fifth floor wax.name: Fifth Floor Wax
fifth floor wax.description: Pooled wax under a sconce — the fifth floor's guaranteed refill.

page — the bitten.name: Page — The Bitten
page — the bitten.description: A torn page in an archivist's hand.
page — the bitten.read_text: "...the bitten one carries a candle she never lights. Ask her why, and she will tell you the price of the way instead. Where there are webs there are spiders; where there is a bite there is a mouth."

fourth floor stair door.name: Fourth Floor Stair Door
fourth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the stair down to the third floor. Locked.

fourth floor wax.name: Fourth Floor Wax
fourth floor wax.description: Pooled, re-hardened wax — the fourth floor's guaranteed refill.

page — the borrowed door.name: Page — The Borrowed Door
page — the borrowed door.description: A torn page, scratched over with a warning.
page — the borrowed door.read_text: "...a survivor who reaches the door first leaves it ajar a little while — longer if they love you, shorter if the tower has turned. Slip out in another's wake and you will not have earned the dark outside."

third floor stair door.name: Third Floor Stair Door
third floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the stair down to the second floor. Locked.

third floor wax.name: Third Floor Wax
third floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the third floor's guaranteed refill.

second floor stair door.name: Second Floor Stair Door
second floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the stair down to the first floor. Locked.

second floor wax.name: Second Floor Wax
second floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the second floor's guaranteed refill.

first floor key.name: First Floor Key
first floor key.description: The ground-floor iron key — the bow that opens the exit. The reliable way out, and the only one that is fully your own.

the exit door.name: The Exit Door
the exit door.description: Heavy, iron-bound, and locked. The only way out. It does not open to the dark, and it does not open to another's passing — only to the key, and to your own light.

first floor wax.name: First Floor Wax
first floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the first floor's guaranteed refill.

matches (fifth).name: Matches (Fifth)
matches (fifth).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread.

matches (fourth).name: Matches (Fourth)
matches (fourth).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread.

matches (third).name: Matches (Third)
matches (third).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread.

matches (second).name: Matches (Second)
matches (second).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread.

matches (first).name: Matches (First)
matches (first).description: Six matches bound with waxed thread.

page — the weather.name: Page — The Weather
page — the weather.description: A torn page pinned behind a portrait whose eyes no longer follow it.
page — the weather.read_text: "...he is the weather now. When you are cruel the sky darkens toward him; when you are kind it eases. You do not summon the storm. You are the storm."

page — the key.name: Page — The Key
page — the key.description: A torn page on a feasting table, under a plate no one has lifted in years.
page — the key.read_text: "...every floor keeps one key, and every key sits in a room built to be safe. The tower is cruel, but it is not unfair. The unfairness is the dark between the rooms."

page — the torpor.name: Page — The Torpor
page — the torpor.description: A torn page in the dust of a coffin room.
page — the torpor.read_text: "...here the tower sleeps, and it wants you to sleep with it. Sloth is the kindest sin; it asks for nothing but the light you are already spending."

page — the last muster.name: Page — The Last Muster
page — the last muster.description: A torn page near the exit, held down by an old weapon.
page — the last muster.read_text: "...he does not guard the door. He has no need. Everything the tower holds gathers at the threshold and waits to see whether your light outlasts your fear."
